title: Bochner majorant estimate, linearity and almost-everywhere congruence
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $(Z,\Sigma,\rho)$ be a measure space and $E$ a complex Banach space. Almost everywhere strongly measurable means equal almost everywhere to a pointwise limit of measurable finite-image simple functions. A function $f:Z\to E$ is Bochner integrable when it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and $\int_Z\|f(z)\|\,d\rho(z)<\infty$. If $f$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable, $g:Z\to\mathbf R$ is integrable, and $\|f(z)\|\leq g(z)$ for almost every $z$, then $f$ is Bochner integrable and $$\left\|\int_Z f\,d\rho\right\|\leq\int_Z g\,d\rho.$$ For Bochner integrable $f_1,f_2:Z\to E$ and $c\in\mathbf C$, $$\int_Z(f_1+f_2)\,d\rho=\int_Z f_1\,d\rho+\int_Z f_2\,d\rho,\qquad\int_Z cf_1\,d\rho=c\int_Z f_1\,d\rho.$$ If $u,v:Z\to E$ agree almost everywhere, their Bochner integrals agree (with the integral defined to be zero for nonintegrable functions).
